         v.

    ESTER M. MCCULLOUGH, et al.,

                          Defendants.

11       Plaintiffs1 and Plaintiff Intervenors2 in this consolidated case challenge the Bureau 
12  of  Land  Management  of  the  U.S.  Department  of  Interior’s3  approval  of  Intervenor-
13  Defendant Lithium Nevada Corporation’s plan to build a lithium mine near Thacker Pass, 
14  Nevada via a January 15, 2021 Record of Decision under the Administrative Procedure 
15  Act, 5 U.S.C. § 701, et seq., the National Environmental Policy Act, 42 U.S.C. §§ 4321-
16  61, the Federal Land Policy and Management Act, 43 U.S.C. §§ 1701-1787, and the 
17  National Historic Preservation Act, 54 U.S.C. § 300101, et seq. (ECF Nos. 1, 46, 83.) See 
18  also Western Watersheds Project, et al. v. Bureau of Land Management of the U.S. 
19  Department of the Interior, et al., Case No. 3:21-cv-00103-MMD-CLB, ECF No. 1 (D. Nev. 
20  Filed Feb. 26, 2021) (since consolidated into this case). Before the Court is the Report 
21  and Recommendation (“R&R” or “Recommendation”) of United States Magistrate Judge 
22  Carla  L.  Baldwin  (ECF  No.  222),  recommending  the  People  be  dismissed  without 
23  prejudice for failure to retain counsel. The People had until May 19, 2022, to file an 
24                                                                       
        1Bartell Ranch LLC and Edward Bartell, along with Western Watersheds Project, 
25  Wildlands Defense, Great Basin Resource Watch, and Basin and Range Watch. 

26                                                                       
        2Reno-Sparks Indian Colony, the Burns Paiute Tribe, and Atsa Koodakuh Wyh 
27  Nuwu/People of Red Mountain (the “People”).                          

28       3Ester M. McCullough, the District Manager of BLM’s Winnemucca office, along 
 1 || objection.  To  date,  no  objection  to  the  R&R  has  been  filed.  For this  reason,  and  as 
2 || explained below, the Court adopts the R&R, and will dismiss the People from this case 
3 || without prejudice. 
4          The  Court  “may  accept,  reject,  or  modify,  in  whole  or  in  part,  the  findings  or 
5 || recommendations made by the magistrate judge.” 28 U.S.C. § 636(b)(1). Where a party 
6 ||  fails  to  object  to  a  magistrate judge’s  recommendation,  the  Court  is  not  required  to 
7 || conduct “any review at all. . . of any issue that is not the subject of an objection.” Thomas 
8 ||  v. Arn, 474 U.S. 140, 149 (1985); see also United States v. Reyna-Tapia, 328 F.3d 1114, 
9 |}  1116  (9th  Cir.  2003)  (“De  novo  review  of  the  magistrate  judges’  findings  and 
10 || recommendations  is  required  if,  but only if,  one  or  both  parties  file  objections  to  the 
11 ||  findings  and  recommendations.”)  (emphasis  in  original);  Fed.  R.  Civ.  P.  72,  Advisory 
12 || Committee Notes (1983) (providing that the Court “need only satisfy itself that there is no 
13 || clear error on the face of the record in order to accept the recommendation.”). 
14          Because there is no objection, the Court need not conduct de novo review, and is 
15 || satisfied Judge Baldwin  did not clearly err.  Here, Judge  Baldwin recommends that the 
16 || People be dismissed because they have not retained counsel, despite prior warnings that 
17 || they must retain counsel to  remain in this case as a party.  (ECF No. 222 at  1-2.) The 
18 || Court agrees with Judge Baldwin. Having reviewed the R&R and the record in this case, 
19 || the Court will adopt the R&R in full. 
20          It is therefore ordered that Judge  Baldwin’s  Report and  Recommendation  (ECF 
21 || No. 222) is accepted and adopted in full. 
22          It is further ordered  that Atsa  Koodakuh Wyh  Nuwu/People of  Red  Mountain  is 
23 ||  dismissed without prejudice. 
24          DATED THIS 20" Day of May 2022. 
25 

27                                        MIRANDAM.DU-——<—tisS 
28                                        CHIEF UNITED STATES DISTRICT JUDGE
